business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of PC and Console Video Games via Digital Stores

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Convention Between Canada and the United States of America with Respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital, signed August 26, 1980, as amended by subsequent protocols
Convention Between Canada and Japan for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income, signed May 7, 2007
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the European Union

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, and its Regulations; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, Part II; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 12; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2, and associated financial sanctions regulations; Limited Partnerships Act, RSO 1990, c L.8; Business Names Act, RSO 1990, c B.17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c 16. For the LP formation itself, the Ontario Business Registry and the Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery administer the statutory filing and registered office records.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Certificate of Status / Certificate of Good Standing of the corporate General Partner, or equivalent foreign registry certificate for a non-resident corporate General Partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery (if General Partner is an Ontario corporation) or the competent corporate registry of the foreign jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the applicable apostille authority; if the origin state is not party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, full consular legalization through the relevant Canadian mission and Ontario notarial certification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized register of directors, officers and beneficial owners / Certificate of Incumbency of the corporate General Partner, together with identity documents of each individual reaching or controlling a 25% interest
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary and notary public of the jurisdiction in which the General Partner is constituted
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization of the notarized signature, pursuant to the 1961 Apostille Convention or bilateral consular legalization rules

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized consent and acknowledgment of appointment of the Ontario registered office and registered agent for service of process
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ontario licensed registered agent / registered office service provider, notarized before an Ontario notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Ontario notarization only for domestic filing; no apostille is required for filing with the Ontario Business Registry, but foreign counterparties may require apostille under Ontario's implementation of the 1961 Convention

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP and sanctions screening must be completed before incorporation. Screening must cover all general partners, limited partners holding at least 25% limited partnership interest, beneficial owners, directors, officers, controllers, banking counterparties, Steam/Valve and PlayStation store contracting contacts, and downstream payment intermediaries. Databases and authorities to be checked include FINTRAC's politically exposed persons (domestic and foreign PEP) standards, Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists, the Canadian Criminal Code designated entities list, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) SDN List and sectoral sanctions, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, and applicable provincial securities commission cease-trade and enforcement lists. Screenings must be refreshed immediately upon any change in control and no less than annually.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Business Names Act, RSO 1990, c B.17 and the Limited Partnerships Act, RSO 1990, c L.8, the registered legal name of an Ontario limited partnership must be expressed in the English or French language, using the letters of the Latin alphabet with conventional English/French accents. Non-Latin scripts (for example, Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic or Japanese characters) must be transliterated into Latin script for the statutory record. A limited partnership name must contain the designation 'Limited Partnership' or the abbreviation 'L.P.' and may use a French designation as required by applicable bilingual regime.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any trademark or official mark that is confusing with an existing registered Ontario name or a protected intellectual property right
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Ontario Business Registry or its mandatory name search (NUANS) identifies a conflict or rejects a proposed limited partnership name, the applicant, through counsel, must submit a formal written appeal to the Director, Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, Registrar under the Business Names Act and Limited Partnerships Act, within 30 days of rejection, stating the grounds, attaching a corrected NUANS report, evidence of consent from any prior name holder, and evidence of distinctiveness or prior use. If the Director upholds the rejection, judicial review may be sought before the Ontario Divisional Court under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, RSO 1990, c J.1, and the applicable administrative appeal window under that Act is 30 days from the date of the reconsideration decision. A fresh NUANS/name search is required after 90 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: An Ontario limited partnership must at all times have a registered office in Ontario and a registered person authorized to accept service of process. A virtual office or serviced registered office is statutorily permissible for registration and service, provided the registered agent maintains a physical address in Ontario. However, because the business will publish video games through Steam and PlayStation stores and collect sales proceeds from Valve Corporation and Sony Interactive Entertainment platforms, the Canadian Revenue Agency and Ontario tax authorities may evaluate whether the LP possesses real commercial substance in Ontario. Accordingly, a virtual office alone, without local management activities, physical or server-based assets in Canada, and genuine commercial substance, could expose the partnership to audit challenges under the anti-avoidance rules in section 245 of the Income Tax Act, RSC 1985 (5th Supp), c 1, and potential L.P. registration revocation proceedings.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk. For a digitally-native publisher operating primarily through a registered agent and virtual office, the annual probability of an unannounced CRA or Ontario tax audit inspection is approximately 2% if the entity has no payroll, no physical occupancy and a modest revenue profile. If the partnership registers for GST/HST, reaches annual taxable revenue above C$30,000, or engages in regular intercompany or cross-border payments with Valve or Sony, the likelihood of a CRA verification or on-site inspection rises to approximately 5-8% per year, and a materially higher probability if other audit indicators, such as unreported UBO changes, are present.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Ontario limited partnership filing fee tariff under the Limited Partnerships Act, RSO 1990, c L.8 and applicable Ontario business registry fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and Ontario registered agent services for the initial 12-month term
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for registered office service and service-of-process acceptance in Toronto or other Ontario jurisdiction

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public of the foreign jurisdiction and the applicable apostille / consular authentication authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial fee plus official authentication and apostille tariff of the state of origin

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO / AML / CFT database screening, PEP and sanctions list verification for all partners, controllers and beneficiaries

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Commercial database license and analyst time; market benchmark of 6-8 hours at prevailing rates

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Ontario pre-incorporation legal review of limited partnership agreement, statutory filing, foreign General Partner documentation and cross-border Steam/PlayStation commercial payout terms
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed pre-incorporation legal fee quoted in US dollars, based on market rates for technology / media corporate work

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.8, ss. 2 (registration requirement), 4 (declaration filing), 9 (liability of limited partners); Partnership Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. P.5; Income Tax Act (Canada), s. 96 (partnership pass-through taxation)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, Companies and Personal Property Security Branch
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. Limited partners may contribute cash or property; Form 1 must state the amount contributed or agreed to be contributed by each limited partner. No escrow account is statutorily mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner adopts the Limited Partnership Agreement and approves formation of the Ontario limited partnership; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the General Partner executes and files Form 1 – Declaration of Limited Partnership with the Ontario Companies and Personal Property Security Branch including capital contribution particulars; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office is fixed at [address], and the following persons are appointed initial officers of the General Partner with authority to open bank accounts, execute Steam/console publishing agreements, and receive subscription proceeds; FURTHER RESOLVED, that one signature of the General Partner is sufficient for filings and banking, and that this resolution remains effective upon official registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and NUANS Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery – Ontario Business Registry / NUANS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Order a NUANS name search report for the proposed limited partnership name and verify that the name is distinctive, not confusingly similar to an existing Ontario corporation or trademark, and does not contain prohibited words. If no name is used, submit the future Ontario Business Registry number as a numbered entity designation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NUANS report reveals a conflict, revise the name and re-run the search; if the name is refused for prohibited terms, submit a formal written consent or choose a non-conflicting alternative.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner and limited partners (private execution; no government filing at this step)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Limited Partnership Agreement covering capital commitments, profit and loss allocations, distribution rules, transfer restrictions, management authority of the General Partner, indemnification, dissolution events, and tax pass-through provisions. Execute the agreement and attach subscription agreements and capital contribution schedules.
required_dossiers: Subscription agreements for each limited partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If terms are later found defective, execute a supplemental deed amending the agreement with unanimous partner consent; no registry filing is required unless the amendment changes mandatory declaration particulars.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Companies and Personal Property Security Branch via Ontario Business Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and execute Form 1 – Declaration of Limited Partnership, listing the General Partner(s), the principal place of business in Ontario, and the actual or agreed capital contributions of each limited partner. Submit the form online or in person, pay the prescribed filing fee, and obtain the official Ontario limited partnership registration record and registration number.
required_dossiers: Proof of Ontario registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is queried or rejected, correct the discrepancies and re-file within 15 days; if mandatory particulars change after registration, file a supplementary declaration rather than revising the original instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency – Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the Ontario limited partnership registration record to obtain a federal Business Number (BN). Register for GST/HST if taxable supplies exceed the $30,000 threshold, open a payroll deduction account if employees will be hired, and register the partnership for annual T5013 information return reporting.
required_dossiers: Canadian contact address and banking details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects or delays registration, contact the CRA Business Enquiries line, correct the registration data through CRA My Business Account, and provide supplemental partnership documentation on request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal licensing department in the registered-office municipality (e.g., Toronto Municipal Licensing and Standards)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm whether the municipality requires a general business licence for an office-based software publishing activity. Digital PC and console game publishing via Steam and PlayStation Store does not require a provincial operating permit; however, a physical administrative office may trigger a local business licence requirement depending on municipal by-laws.
required_dossiers: Commercial lease or ownership deed for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a municipal licence is refused, apply for a variance or request reconsideration through the municipal licensing committee; if the dispute persists, seek judicial review under the applicable municipal by-law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Partnership Bank Account and Configure Payment Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banking institution in Canada (e.g., BMO, TD, RBC, CIBC, Scotiabank), branch compliance department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Provide the partnership registration record, limited partnership agreement, the entered board resolution, and identification of all authorized signatories. Open a CDN/USD partnership account and configure the banking details for Steamworks payout and PlayStation Store partner payout by submitting the SWIFT/ABA/account numbers to the respective platform partner dashboards.
required_dossiers: Board resolution of the General Partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional KYC documents, provide revised organizational charts or source-of-funds declarations; if the account is declined, present the matter to the branch compliance officer or apply at another major Canadian bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Statutory Filings and Annual Maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Companies and Personal Property Security Branch and Canada Revenue Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain a registered office in Ontario and keep the partnership declaration current. File the prescribed annual return with the Ontario registry, notify the registry of any change of address or general partner within the statutory period, and file the annual T5013 partnership information return with CRA.
required_dossiers: General Partner resolution on any governance changes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a filing is rejected for lateness or inaccuracy, pay the late fee and file an amended declaration or supplementary declaration; if the partnership is struck off, apply for reinstatement through the Ontario Business Registry.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no manufacturing or physical production facility; digital software publishing is not a licensable industrial activity in Ontario
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — Steam and PlayStation Store publishing requires commercial agreements with the platform operators, not a provincial operating license

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — pure software publishing uses no manufacturing, no stationary combustion source, and no wastewater discharge; no Environmental Impact Assessment is required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — no wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste streams are generated. If a physical office is later leased, standard municipal waste disposal bylaws and Ontario Fire Code compliance apply; no EPA or provincial ECA permit is required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable to a virtual digital publishing business. If a physical office is occupied, the premises must comply with the Ontario Fire Code (O. Reg. 213/07), general building code structural load requirements for office occupancy, and workplace health and safety obligations under the Occupational Health and Safety Act (R.S.O. 1990, c. O.1).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Canadian limited partnerships register for a Business Number (BN) via the CRA online portal or Form RC1. Foreign entities must register with the CRA to obtain a statutory TIN equivalent (BN) and GST/HST number if carrying on business in Canada through a permanent establishment. Subsequent compliance includes filing T3 Partnership Returns and allocating income to partners.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Limited partnerships may elect to be treated as corporations for income tax purposes under subsection 9(5) of the Income Tax Act by filing Form T2052 with the CRA. Hybrid mismatch and other tax treaty elections are available under the Multilateral Instrument.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in aggregate taxable supplies during a calendar year
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time digital reporting and clearance through the CRA GST/HST e-services platform, including API integration for invoice data submission and electronic stamping for qualifying transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated supplies include exports of goods and services to non-residents outside Canada. For digital goods such as video game software distributed via platforms, eligibility requires delivery and consumption outside Canada, supported by contractual terms, payment records, and delivery logs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits may scrutinize export claims; fraudulent claims result in 200% penalty on the zero-rated tax plus interest, with potential prosecution under the Excise Tax Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); with the Department of Finance Canada (Exchange Fund Account) and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) administering related regulatory and AML functions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full convertibility for current and capital account transactions, consistent with IMF Article VIII status under the Bretton Woods Agreements Act. The Canadian dollar is freely floated; there is no framework requiring central bank approval for capital inflow or outflow or for profit remittance. Non-resident limited partners may receive distributive cash flows provided Canadian tax filings, including partnership information returns and applicable treaty relief, are properly completed; no exchange control certificate is necessary.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada has no statutory rules requiring surrender, repatriation, or conversion of export proceeds. All export receipts, including USD proceeds from Valve/PlayStation store sales, may be held in USD corporate accounts or converted freely. Mandatory conversion ratio: 0%. Statutory timeline: none.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as a supplemental multi-currency collection or disbursement wallet; Low as a replacement for a regulated Canadian corporate bank account. An offshore digital EMI is not authorized under the Bank Act (Canada) and cannot accept deposits or provide LVTS settlement in Canada. A foreign EMI may process Steam/PlayStation payouts and FX conversion through its own correspondent arrangements if it is a licensed money services business in Canada or registered under the Retail Payment Activities Act; the core treasury liquidity account must remain with a Canadian Schedule I bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A statutory universal requirement for all directors to appear physically does not exist under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. In practice, Canadian Schedule I banks require at least one authorized signatory and every beneficial owner holding 25% or more to complete in-person or bank-approved remote video identity verification. Non-resident limited partners and the general partner should expect a physical or live-video compliance interview, notarized corporate documentation, and certified copies of passports and proof of address before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Limited partnership general partner is not a Canadian tax resident or has no physical office in Ontario.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ontario Certificate of Limited Partnership from the Ontario Business Registry; executed Limited Partnership Agreement; general partner identification (passport and proof of address); non-resident partner list; office lease in Ontario; staffing evidence; audited financial statements; legal opinion confirming active Ontario-based game publishing operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cyclical digital-platform receipts from Valve and PlayStation with thousands of low-value consumer transactions do not match ordinary invoices.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform settlement reports and payout statements; monthly reconciliation ledger matching platform statements to accounting entries and bank deposits; Steam and PlayStation publishing agreements; revenue recognition policy; AML self-assessment; fully auditable audit trail including transaction-level records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Immediate onward wires to contractors, engine licensors, or vendors in unlisted or high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening logs; counterparty due-diligence files; executed contracts and invoices evidencing real services; OFAC/UN/Canadian sanctions list search results; board-approved anti-money-laundering policy; confirmation that no anonymity-enhanced cryptocurrencies are used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners with minimal capital contributions but expected high distributions, raising round-tripping or tax evasion suspicions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital contribution receipts and bank statements; contribution schedules; T5013 partnership information returns; distribution policy approval minutes; list of substantive business assets and employees; legal opinion confirming tax compliance and absence of sham transaction indicia.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership is indirect through layered holding companies or trusts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial ownership register; full organizational chart; trust deeds or holding company constitutional documents; natural-person ultimate owner declarations; FATCA/CRS self-certifications; PEP screening results; certified corporate records from every intermediate entity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital must enter through a designated Canadian bank account using SWIFT MT103; CAD is settled through LVTS and USD through US correspondent Fedwire/CHIPS. The remitter must include the purpose narrative 'Capital Contribution - LP Agreement dated [date]', a unique contribution notice reference, and the restricted capital account number. The bank will require the LP Agreement, Certificate of Limited Partnership, beneficial owner identification, source-of-funds evidence, and a funds-flow diagram before final settlement. There is no Canadian central bank approval for inward remittance, but FINTRAC's $10,000 electronic funds transfer reporting rule applies to certain large transfers and banks must maintain full audit records.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for outbound trade disbursements are: (1) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border wires; (2) LVTS for domestic CAD payments; (3) Fedwire/CHIPS for USD cross-border payments; and (4) Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit for high-value procurement, where payment is made against presentation of compliant documents. Platform proceeds from Valve and PlayStation are collected through platform payout rails and cleared into the CAD/USD operational account; export proceeds surrender rules do not apply. All outbound wires must carry an economic-purpose narrative and undergo OFAC/sanctions screening; Part XIII withholding documentation must be retained for payments to non-residents.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD deliverable forward contracts with a Canadian Schedule I bank or OSFI-regulated dealer
Non-deliverable forward contracts (NDFs) limited to hedges in non-CAD non-convertible currencies; CAD/USD is onshore deliverable and physical settlement is standard
Cross-currency swaps for converting USD-denominated platform receivables into CAD-denominated operating cash flows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: ServiceOntario – Companies and Personal Property Security Branch
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may render the limited partnership incapable of maintaining legal proceedings; continued default permits the Director to cancel registration, resulting in loss of limited-liability protection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (including T5013 Summary and Partner Schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For December 31 fiscal year-end: March 31 if all partners are Canadian residents; June 30 if any partner is non-resident. For fiscal years ending other than December 31: within 3 months after year-end for all-resident partnerships; within 6 months after year-end if any non-resident partner.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of the greater of CAD 100 or CAD 25 per partner per day, to a maximum of CAD 2,500; additional penalties apply for missing or incorrect T5013 slips.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for an Ontario limited partnership under the Limited Partnerships Act or the Income Tax Act solely by virtue of partnership status. An independent audit may become contractually required by the limited partnership agreement, a lender, or securities regulators if the partnership distributes ownership interests or becomes a reporting issuer.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian tax records must be maintained under Income Tax Act section 230. If financial statements are prepared, they may follow IFRS or ASPE in accordance with the partnership agreement; these standards are not statutorily mandated for a non-reporting limited partnership.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Ontario limited partnerships are not subject to corporate UBO (individuals with significant control) filing duties. The annual declaration confirms the names and addresses of all general partners and the principal place of business; any change in limited or general partners or in capital contributions is reported by filing an amended declaration with ServiceOntario. No annual confirmation is required for transfers of limited partnership interests beyond updating the partnership's internal records.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (names, addresses, capital contributions)
Copies of initial and amended Limited Partnership Declarations

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at Ontario limited partnership entity level (fiscally transparent pass-through); combined federal-Ontario headline corporate income tax rate of 26.5% (federal 15.0% + Ontario 11.5%) applies to income allocated to corporate partners in the year of allocation.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Ontario Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit (OIDMTC) refundable at 40% of qualifying Ontario labour expenditures for eligible interactive digital media products; federal SR&ED investment tax credit 35% refundable (CCPC partners) / 15% non-refundable (non-CCPC corporate partners); Ontario Innovation Tax Credit (10%).
